record.title: Two-color conjecture for strong local irregularity of digraphs
record.statement:
For a digraph $D$, define the balanced degree of a vertex $x$ by

$$
\sigma(x)=d^+(x)-d^-(x).
$$

A digraph is strongly locally irregular if $\sigma(x)\neq\sigma(y)$ for every arc $xy$, and let $\mathrm{slir}(D)$ be the minimum number of colors in an arc coloring whose color classes induce strongly locally irregular digraphs. **Strong local irregularity conjecture.** Every digraph $D$ satisfies

$$
\mathrm{slir}(D)\leq 2.
$$

The source notes that strong local irregularity is not directly controlled by the corresponding notion for orientations of simple graphs and presents the statement as an open conjecture supported by the paper’s investigation.

record.title: Conjecture that the two repetition ratios agree
record.statement:
For each minimum degree $\delta\geq4$, let $f(\delta)$ and $f'(\delta)$ denote the two repetition ratios defined in the paper for the diameter problem under the relevant clique- or chromatic-number condition.

**Repetition-ratio conjecture.** For every $\delta\geq4$,

$$
f(\delta)=f'(\delta).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the exact computations for $\delta=4,5,6$, where the optimal repeatable graphs have equal chromatic and clique numbers; the supplied text gives no resolution for general $\delta$.
record.source_name: Stijn Cambie and Jorik Jooken, “Sharp results for the Erdős, Pach, Pollack and Tuza problem”, arXiv:2502.08626 (2025).

record.title: Reed's recolouring conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, with clique number $4\omega(G)4$ and maximum degree $4\Delta(G)4$. A proper $k$-colouring is **Kempe-recolourable** when it can be transformed through Kempe changes, which interchange two colours on a connected component of the subgraph induced by those colours.

**Reed's recolouring conjecture.** Any graph $G$ is $k$-recolourable for all

$$
k \geqslant \left\lceil \frac{1}{3}\omega(G) + \frac{2}{3}(\Delta(G) +1) \right\rceil.
$$

The conjecture is a recolouring analogue of Reed's conjecture that the chromatic number is at most $\left\lceil(\omega(G)+\Delta(G)+1)/2\right\rceil$. The paper proves that frozen colourings are unique up to permuting colours below this threshold, while constructions show the bound is tight; the recolouring assertion remains open.

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2025). “As a consequence of (respectively ), note that disproving (respectively ) would require new tools and would significantly improve our understanding of Kempe recolouring and its obstruc”

record.title: Recolouring conjecture for triangle-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a triangle-free graph, let $\Delta(G)$ be its maximum degree, and let $k$ denote the number of colours in a proper colouring. A colouring is **Kempe-recolourable** when it can be transformed by Kempe changes, interchanging two colours on a connected bichromatic component.

**Triangle-free recolouring conjecture.** Any triangle-free graph $G$ is $k$-recolourable for all

$$
k \geqslant \left\lceil \frac{4}{9}\cdot 2 + \frac{5}{9}(\Delta(G) +1) \right\rceil.
$$

The threshold is motivated by the paper's optimal analysis of frozen-colouring obstructions in triangle-free graphs, and the conjecture is tight in view of constructions above the threshold. The recolouring statement itself remains open.

record.title: Gu–Jia–Wu conjecture on chords of longest cycles through an edge
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $3$-connected graph and let $e$ be an edge of $G$. Among the cycles containing $e$, call one **longest** if it has maximum length among all cycles containing $e$.

**Gu–Jia–Wu conjecture.** Every longest cycle containing $e$ has a chord.

This conjecture is a local, edge-prescribed strengthening of the general question about chords in longest cycles. The source presents it as a conjecture proposed in 2005; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: The minimum-degree conjecture for majority edge colourings
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph. A **$1/k$-majority edge colouring** with colour set $C$ is an edge colouring $omega:E\to C$ such that, for every vertex $v$ and colour $c\in C$, the number $d_{E_c}(v)$ of incident edges coloured $c$ satisfies $d_{E_c}(v)\leq d(v)/k$. 

**Majority edge-colouring conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq 2$, if a graph $G$ has minimum degree $\delta\geq k^2$, then $G$ is $1/k$-majority edge $(k+1)$-colourable.

The bound is best possible up to the stated threshold because, for every $k\geq 2$, there is a graph of minimum degree $k^2-1$ without such a colouring. The conjecture is known for $k=2,3,4$ and for bipartite graphs, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Paweł Pękała and Jakub Przybyło, “On list extensions of the majority edge colourings”, arXiv:2502.12688 (2025).
record.references:

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2025).

record.title: The list strengthening of the minimum-degree conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph. An **$\ell$-list assignment** is a map $L:E\to 2^C$ with $|L(e)|=\ell$ for every edge. An $L$-colouring is an edge colouring using a colour from each edge's list, and it is a **$1/k$-majority edge colouring** if $d_{E_c}(v)\leq d(v)/k$ for every vertex $v$ and colour $c$.

**List strengthening conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq 2$, if a graph $G$ has minimum degree $\delta(G)\geq k^2$, then $G$ has a $1/k$-majority edge colouring from any lists of size $k+1$.

This directly strengthens the minimum-degree conjecture for unrestricted colours and is supported by the regular-graph result proved in the paper. The general statement remains open.

record.title: Minimum Fourier entropy–influence conjecture
record.statement:
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function. Its minimum Fourier entropy and total influence are

$$
\operatorname{\mathbf{H}}_{\infty}(f)=\min_{S\subset[n]}\log\frac{1}{|\widehat f(S)|^2},\qquad \operatorname{\mathbf{I}}(f)=\sum_{S\subset[n]}|\widehat f(S)|^2|S|.
$$

**Minimum Fourier entropy–influence conjecture.** There exists a constant $c>0$ such that, for every $n$ and every Boolean function $f$,

$$
\operatorname{\mathbf{H}}_{\infty}(f)\leq c\operatorname{\mathbf{I}}(f).
$$

This is the minimum-entropy analogue of the Fourier entropy–influence conjecture. The supplied excerpt gives no resolution status or additional evidence, so the conjecture is recorded as open.

record.title: Bírógyiköğlü–Hordijk–Leydold–Pisanski–Stadler conjecture on strong nodal domains of hypercubes
record.statement:
Let $H(n,2)$ be the Hamming graph with vertex set $\mathbb{Z}_2^n$, where two vertices are adjacent when they differ in exactly one coordinate. Its Laplacian has eigenvalue $2i$ for $0\leq i\leq n$. For an eigenfunction $f$, let $\mathrm{SND}(f)$ denote its number of strong nodal domains.

**Bírógyiköğlü–Hordijk–Leydold–Pisanski–Stadler conjecture.** For every $1\leq i\leq n-2$, there is an eigenfunction $f$ of $H(n,2)$ with eigenvalue $2i$ such that $\mathrm{SND}(f)=2$.

The conjecture extends the known result for $1\leq i\leq n/2$ and concerns the minimum possible number of strong nodal domains of hypercube eigenfunctions. The paper confirms it for $i$ up to approximately $2n/3$, while the remaining cases require a new approach.

record.title: Győri's asymptotic clique-packing conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph. For $r\text{ fixed}$, write $
u_r(G)$ for the maximum number of edge-disjoint $r$-cliques in $G$, and let $t_{r-1}(n)$ denote the number of edges in the Turán graph with $r-1$ parts. If $k\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfies

$$
e(G)=t_{r-1}(n)+k,
$$

**Győri's conjecture.** For every fixed $r\geq 3$,

$$
\nu_r(G)\geq \frac{(2-o(1))k}{r}.
$$

This conjecture asymptotically strengthens the Győri–Tuza bound on decomposing the edges of a graph into $2$-cliques and $r$-cliques, and extends the expected statement to $r=3$.

record.title: The bounded blocky-matrix complexity conjecture for bounded max-norm
record.statement: Let $M$ be a Boolean matrix, meaning a matrix with entries in $\{0,1\}$. Its factorization max-norm is denoted by $\gamma_2(M)$, and let $\operatorname{bl}(M)$ be the minimum number of blocky matrices whose $\pm1$-linear combination is $M$. **The bounded blocky-matrix complexity conjecture.** For every $\gamma>0$ there exists $b_{\gamma}$ such that every Boolean matrix $M$ with $\gamma_2(M)\leq\gamma$ satisfies $\operatorname{bl}(M)\leq b_{\gamma}$. This conjecture asks for a qualitative converse to the inequality $\gamma_2(M)\leq\operatorname{bl}(M)$ and is equivalent to Conjecture III of HHH. Its resolution status is not specified in the source.

record.title: The large empty bipartite pair conjecture under induced four-cycle-free restrictions
record.statement: Let $G$ be a bipartite graph with vertex classes $A$ and $B$, each of size $n$. The maximum degree of $G$ is at most $\varepsilon n$, and an induced four cycle-free subgraph is an induced subgraph containing no cycle of length four. **The large empty bipartite pair conjecture.** For every $k>0$ there exist $\varepsilon,c>0$ such that, if $G$ contains no induced four cycle-free subgraph of average degree more than $k$, then there exist $X\subset A$ and $Y\subset B$ with $|X|=|Y|\geq cn$ and no edges between $X$ and $Y$. The source states that proving this combinatorial assertion would suffice for the large constant submatrix consequence of the preceding conjecture, but gives no resolution status.

record.title: The bowtie extremal-orientation conjecture
record.statement:
Let $B=F_{2,3}$ be the bowtie graph, with a distinguished center vertex. Let $G$ be a complete tripartite graph with part sizes $1$, $\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor$, and $\left\lceil\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rceil$. Let $\vec{B}$ be an orientation of $B$ as in Case (a) or (b) of the proposition preceding this conjecture. **The bowtie extremal-orientation conjecture.** For every such orientation, 
$$
D(G,\vec{B})=D(n,\vec{B}).
$$
 This conjecture identifies a complete tripartite graph as an extremal host for the specified unresolved orientations of the bowtie; the preceding proposition shows that these orientations have more than $2^{\mathrm{ex}(n,B)}$ orientations in general, while the exact value remains open.

record.title: Extremal cubic graph conjecture for the subpath number
record.statement: Assume that $n\geq 10$ is even. If $n=4q-2$ for some integer $q$, let $L_n$ be obtained from $(n-10)/4$ copies of $K_4-e$ by adding $(n-10)/4-1$ edges so that the resulting graph is connected and has maximum degree $3$. If $n=4q$, let $L_n$ be obtained from $(n-12)/4$ copies of $K_4-e$ connected into a path-like structure in the same way, with pendant blocks on $5$ and $7$ vertices. The **extremal cubic graph conjecture.** In the class of cubic graphs on $n$ vertices, the graph $L_n$ is the only graph which minimizes the subpath number. The conjecture proposes the unique minimizer among cubic graphs of even order $n\geq 10$. The source does not provide evidence of resolution.

record.title: Chan–Pak conjecture on the log-concavity of minimum positions in linear extensions
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite poset, let $A\subseteq P$, and let $\ell$ be a uniformly random linear extension of $P$. Define

$$
\ell_{\min}(A)=\min\{\ell(a):a\in A\}.
$$

**Chan–Pak conjecture.** For every $A\subseteq P$, the sequence of probabilities of the minimum position is log-concave:

$$
\P[\ell_{\min}(A)=k]^2 \geq \P[\ell_{\min}(A)=k-1]\cdot\P[\ell_{\min}(A)=k+1].
$$

This conjecture generalizes Stanley's log-concavity theorem, recovered when $|A|=1$. The source presents it as a conjecture, and no resolution is supplied here.

record.title: Dahlberg–She–van Willigenburg's non-e-positivity conjecture for trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, let $\Delta(T)$ denote its maximum degree, and say that $T$ is **$e$-positive** when its chromatic symmetric function $X_T$ has a nonnegative expansion in the elementary symmetric-function basis. **Dahlberg–She–van Willigenburg's conjecture.** If

$$
\Delta(T)\geq 4,
$$

then $T$ is not $e$-positive. This conjecture links the structure of a tree to positivity properties of its chromatic symmetric function. It was verified for all trees with maximum degree at least $5$ and for spiders with maximum degree $4$, but the general case remains open.

record.title: The Nordhaus–Gaddum full Brouwer conjecture for Laplacian spectra
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, let $\overline{G}$ be its complement, and let $s_k(G)$ denote the sum of the $k$ largest Laplacian eigenvalues of $G$. **Nordhaus–Gaddum full Brouwer conjecture.** For every $k\in\{1,2,\cdots,n-1\}$,

$$
s_k(G)+s_k(\overline{G})\leq\binom{n}{2}+2\binom{k+1}{2},
$$

with equality if and only if $G$ is a threshold graph having $n=2k+1$ vertices and clique number $k+1$. This is proposed as a Nordhaus–Gaddum analogue of the full Brouwer conjecture; the source presents only partial solutions, so the general assertion remains open.

record.title: The antimagic threshold characterization for unions with paths on three vertices
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, let $P_3$ be the path on three vertices, and let $\tau(G)$ be the maximum integer such that the disjoint union of $G$ and $c$ copies of $P_3$ is antimagic for every integer $c$ with $0\le c\le\tau(G)$; if $G$ is not antimagic, set $\tau(G)=-\infty$. A graph is **antimagic** if it has a bijective edge labeling by $\{1,2,\ldots,|E(G)|\}$ whose vertex sums are pairwise distinct. **Threshold characterization.** For a graph $G$, the union of $G$ and $c$ copies of $P_3$ is antimagic if and only if $c\le\tau(G)$. This conjecture concerns the precise threshold for adding copies of $P_3$ to a graph; the supplied text gives no resolution status or further evidence beyond presenting it as a proposed statement.

record.title: Eventual saturation number for cycles of lengths from 4 to r
record.statement:
For a positive integer set $I$, let $\mathcal{C}_I$ denote the family of cycles whose lengths belong to $I$, and let $\operatorname{sat}(n,\mathcal{C}_I)$ be the minimum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $\mathcal{C}_I$-saturated graph. **The conjecture.** For any integer $r
a 5$, there exists a number $n(r)$ such that for any integer $n
a n(r)$,

$$
\operatorname{sat}(n, \mathcal{C}_{[4,r]})=\left\lceil\frac{5n}{4}-\frac{3}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

The paper establishes the corresponding formula for $I=\{4,5\}$ and for $I=[4,+\infty)$, but the assertion for every finite upper endpoint $r$ remains open.

record.title: Bukh–Borisov deletion-distance conjecture for binary words
record.statement:
For a binary word $W$, let $g(W)$ be the minimum number of letters that must be deleted from $W$ to obtain a shuffle square, and let $g(n)$ be the maximum of $g(W)$ over binary words of length $n$. A **shuffle square** is a word containing two disjoint equal subsequences whose total length is the word's length.

**Bukh–Borisov deletion-distance conjecture.** There is a constant $c$ such that, for every $n$, 

$$
g(n)\geqslant c\sqrt n,
$$

that is, there exists a binary word of length $n$ with largest twins leaving out at least $c\sqrt n$ elements.

Known bounds include $g(n)=o(n)$ and $g(n)=\Omega(n^{1/3})$. The conjecture predicts the stronger lower bound of order $\sqrt n$.

record.title: Erdős's lower-bound conjecture for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers
record.statement:
Let $r(s,t)$ denote the minimum integer $n$ such that every red-blue coloring of the edges of the complete graph on $n$ vertices contains a red copy of $K_s$ or a blue copy of $K_t$. **Erdős's conjecture.** For all $s \geq 4$, there exists $c=c(s)>0$ such that

$$
r(s,t) \geq \frac{t^{s-1}}{(\log t)^c}.
$$

This conjecture predicts the expected polynomial order of off-diagonal Ramsey numbers up to a power of a logarithm. The paper notes that the case $s=4$ is resolved by the stated bounds for $r(4,t)$, while the general case remains open.

record.title: Erdős's cycle-complete Ramsey conjecture for C4
record.statement:
Let $r(C_4,t)$ denote the minimum integer $n$ such that every $C_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices contains an independent set of size $t$. **Erdős's $C_4$ Ramsey conjecture.** There exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $t$,

$$
r(C_4,t)\leq t^{2-\varepsilon}.
$$

This is described as one of the most challenging open conjectures in Ramsey theory. It asks for a polynomial improvement over the quadratic upper bound for the cycle-complete-graph Ramsey number.

record.title: The Erdős–Rogers function asymptotic conjecture
record.statement:
For integers $t>s\geq2$, let $f_{s,t}(n)$ be the largest integer $m$ such that every $n$-vertex $K_t$-free graph has an induced $K_s$-free subgraph with at least $m$ vertices. **The Erdős–Rogers function conjecture.** For all $s\geq3$, as $n\to\infty$,

$$
f_{s,s+1}(n)=\sqrt n\,(\log n)^{1-o(1)}.
$$

The source presents this as a tentative conjecture, contrasting it with the known order of magnitude of $f_{2,3}(n)$. The supplied status evidence proves this statement, so its database status is solved.

record.title: Laborde–Payan–Xuong conjecture on independent sets meeting longest paths
record.statement: Let $D$ be a digraph, and call a set of vertices **independent** if no two of its vertices are joined by an arc. A path in $D$ is **longest** if it has maximum length among all paths in $D$. **Laborde–Payan–Xuong conjecture.** Every digraph has an independent set meeting every longest path. The conjecture is presented as an open problem from 1983; the paper does not state a resolution in the supplied text.

record.title: Salia's cycle-cover conjecture for infinite bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph with sides $A$ and $B$. For a subset $X\subseteq V(G)$ with $|X|\geq 2$, let $N^2_G(X)$ be the set of vertices having at least two neighbors in $X$. The graph $G$ has the **double Hall property** if $|N^2_G(X)|\geq |X|$ for every $X\subseteq A$ with $|X|\geq 2$.

**Salia's conjecture.** If $G$ has the double Hall property, then for every $X\subseteq A$ with $|X|\geq 2$ there is a cycle $C_X$ in $G$ such that

$$
V(C_X)\cap A=X.
$$

The conjecture proposes that the double Hall condition is sufficient to find a cycle covering any prescribed finite or infinite subset of $A$ of size at least two, with no other vertices of $A$ on the cycle. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture is recorded as open.

record.title: Conjecture on the minimal orders of ordered and additive factorizations
record.statement:
Let $g(n)$ count ordered factorizations of $n$, let $b(n)$ count the corresponding additive factorizations, and let $a(n)$ be the associated counting function. Let $\rho$ be the constant used in the paper. For positive quantities $f$ and $h$, the notation $f(n)\asymp h(n)$ means that their ratio is bounded above and below by positive constants.

**Minimal-order conjecture.** As $n\to\infty$,

$$
b(n)\asymp n^{\rho-1}\quad\text{for composite }n,
$$

and

$$
a(n)\asymp n^{\rho-1}\quad\text{for all }n.
$$

This concerns the poorly understood minimal orders of the functions $a(n)$ and $b(n)$; the preceding discussion notes that the simple prime values of $b(n)$ do not determine the minimal order of $a(n)$, so these asymptotics remain open.

record.title: Yu's folklore conjecture for Hamming-cube t-codes
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}_n=\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with Hamming distance, and let $A(\mathcal{H}_n,t)$ denote the largest size of a $t$-code in $\mathcal{H}_n$, meaning a set with at most $t$ permitted pairwise distances. **Yu's folklore conjecture.** For every sufficiently large $n$ with respect to $t$,

$$
A(\mathcal{H}_n,t)=A\bigl(\mathcal{H}_n,\{2,4,\dots,2t\}\bigr)=
\begin{cases}
\binom{n}{0}+\binom{n}{2}+\dots+\binom{n}{t-2}+\binom{n}{t},&\text{if $t$ is even},\\
\binom{n}{1}+\binom{n}{3}+\dots+\binom{n}{t-2}+\binom{n}{t},&\text{if $t$ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

This predicts that the maximum is attained by the even-distance set $\{2,4,\ldots,2t\}$; the statement is presented as folklore and remains unresolved in the supplied text.

record.title: Nine-vertex 2-core conjecture for Steiner triple systems
record.statement:
A **Steiner triple system** is a 3-uniform hypergraph in which every pair of vertices lies in exactly one edge. A **2-core** is a hypergraph with minimum degree $2$.

**Nine-vertex 2-core conjecture.** Every sufficiently large Steiner triple system contains a 2-core on nine vertices.

The conjecture is motivated by observations that all Steiner triple systems of size $21$ with a non-trivial automorphism group contain a $3\times 3$ grid, as well as by the Brown–Erdős–Sós conjecture and known results that every Steiner triple system contains a core on at most ten vertices. Its status is open.

record.title: The prime-power sharpness conjecture for k(m)
record.statement: Let $k(m)$ be the maximum number of distinct values of $g_m(n)$ attained at a fixed endpoint in the paper's construction, and let $d(m)$ denote the number of positive divisors of $m$. **Prime-power sharpness conjecture.** For every prime power $m$, the bound $k(m)\leq d(m)-1$ is attained: $k(m)=d(m)-1$. The paper notes sharpness for several examples and for prime $m$, but leaves the assertion for all prime powers open.

record.title: The finiteness conjecture for simultaneous T_m and T'_m values

record.title: The 1/10 upper-bound conjecture for triangle expansions
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph. For $U\subseteq V(G)$, let $G_U$ be obtained by expanding each vertex of $U$ into a triangle, and let $T(G)$ be the minimum size of a set $U$ for which the edge-set of $G_U$ can be covered with four perfect matchings. **The $1/10$ upper-bound conjecture.** Every bridgeless cubic graph $G$ satisfies

$$
T(G)\leq \frac{|V(G)|}{10}.
$$

The paper proves the weaker bound $T(G)\leq \frac{2}{5}|V(G)|$ assuming the 5-cycle double cover conjecture. The proposed bound remains open.

record.title: The density-threshold conjecture for global synchrony
record.statement: A graph is **globally synchronizing** when its adjacency matrix has only synchronized global minima of the Kuramoto energy. **Density-threshold conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist a positive integer $n$ and a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices whose minimum degree is at least $\left(\frac34-\varepsilon\right)n$, but which is not globally synchronizing. The $\frac34$ threshold is supported by known upper bounds and dynamical evidence, but the conjectured extremal construction remains open.

record.title: Automorphism count from companion multiplicities
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a poset with $n$ elements, and let $\mathcal{A}_1,\ldots,\mathcal{A}_k$ be the mutually different collections of type $\mathrm{Comp}(P,\omega)$ for $\omega\in\Sigma_P$. Suppose that $\mathcal{A}_i$ appears for $l_i$ different $P$-listings, so that $l_1+\cdots+l_k=n!$. Let $A(P)$ denote the number of automorphisms of $P$. **Automorphism-count conjecture.** For any poset $P$,

$$
A(P)=\mathrm{min}\{l_i\}.
$$

The preceding discussion establishes the lower bound $A(P)\leq l_i$ for every $i$ and proposes that the smallest companion multiplicity exactly recovers the automorphism count; no resolution is supplied in the excerpt.

record.title: Quadrics base locus conjecture for exceptional dimensions
record.statement:
Let $n\in\{8,16\}$, and let $L\subset\mathbb{R}_{sym}^{n\times n}$ be a subspace satisfying

$$
\boldsymbol{\mathrm{P}}(L)\cap\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Y}}=\varnothing

and such that $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{P}}(L^\vee)\cap\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Z}}$ exists and can span $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{P}}(L^\vee)$. **Quadrics base locus conjecture.** The maximum dimension of $L$ in Theorem is $\frac{1}{2}n$.

The conjecture concerns the unsettled exceptional dimensions $n=8,16$ in the paper's algebraic-geometric decomposition problem. The cases $n=2,4$ are stated to be known, while the optimal dimension remains undetermined for $n=8,16$.

record.title: Erdős's conjecture on the smallest prime divisors of Sierpiński sequences
record.statement: Let $k$ be a Sierpiński number, meaning that $k\cdot 2^n+1$ is composite for every positive integer $n$. For each positive integer $n$, let the smallest prime divisor of $k\cdot 2^n+1$ be the least prime dividing that integer. **Erdős's conjecture.** The smallest prime divisor of $k\cdot 2^n+1$ remains bounded as $n$ tends to infinity. This conjecture concerns whether the prime divisors witnessing the compositeness of a Sierpiński sequence can always be chosen from a bounded set; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status is open.

record.title: Strict monotonicity conjecture for Maker–Breaker clique games
record.statement:
For positive integers $m,b$ and a positive integer $N$, let $f_N(m,b)$ be the largest integer $q$ such that Maker can occupy a clique $K_q$ in the $(m:b)$ Maker–Breaker game played on $K_N$, where Maker claims $m$ edges and Breaker claims $b$ edges per turn.

**Strict monotonicity conjecture.** For fixed $b,m$, for all sufficiently large $N$,

$$
f_N(m,b+1)<f_N(m,b)<f_N(m+1,b),
$$

and both differences tend to infinity as $N\to\infty$.

The source notes that the first inequality for $m=1$ would follow from an unsolved conjecture of Bednarska and Łuczak. The general conjecture is therefore presented as open.

record.title: Independent mutual-visibility coloring conjecture for subdivided complete graphs
record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, let $S(K_n)$ denote its subdivision graph, and let $\chi_{\mu_i}(G)$ be the independent mutual-visibility chromatic number of a graph $G$. Let $\rho(n)$ be the parameter defined in the paper.

**Independent mutual-visibility coloring conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$,

$$
\chi_{\mu_i}\big(S(K_n)\big)=\rho(n)+1.
$$

The preceding results establish that the ordinary mutual-visibility chromatic number of $S(K_n)$ is either $\rho(n)$ or $\rho(n)+1$, while the conjectured exact value for the independent version remains open.

record.title: Self-negative games attain the maximum birthday game size
record.statement:
Let $F(b)$ be the maximum value of $f(X)$ among games $X$ with birthday $b$, and let $-X$ denote the negation of the game $X$. **Self-negation conjecture.** For every integer $b\geq 0$, there exists a game $X$ with birthday $b$ such that $X=-X$ and

$$
f(X)=F(b).
$$

This would show that the maximum game size at each birthday can always be attained by a self-negative game, supporting the proposed family of games in the context of the birthday function. The source does not provide a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

record.title: Bergström's conjecture on the Euclidean Steinitz constant
record.statement:
Let $B_2^d$ denote the Euclidean unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $S(B_2^d)$ be its Steinitz constant: the smallest $C$ such that every finite set of vectors $V\subset B_2^d$ with sum zero admits an ordering whose partial sums have Euclidean norm at most $C$. **Bergström's conjecture.** For all $d\geq 1$, 

$$
S(B_2^d)=O(\sqrt{d}).
$$

This conjecture, known as the Steinitz problem, sought a much stronger estimate than the general bound $S(B)\leq d$. The supplied status evidence says that it has been refuted.

record.title: Linear sumset Ramsey bound in the binary vector space
record.statement:
For $X\subseteq\mathbb F_2^n$, let $\alpha(X)$ denote the maximum dimension of a subspace disjoint from $X$, let $X+X=\{x+y:x,y\in X\}$, and let $\omega(X+X)$ denote the maximum dimension of a subspace contained in $X+X$.

**Linear sumset bound conjecture.** There is a constant $C>0$ such that, for all $n\in\mathbb N$ and every $X\subseteq\mathbb F_2^n$, one has

$$
\max\bigl(\alpha(X),\omega(X+X)\bigr)\ge Cn.
$$

The source notes that this would make the corresponding Ramsey estimate linear in the relevant dimension, improving the proved polynomial bound. Its general validity is open.

record.title: KAMAK tree conjecture for grounded forests
record.statement:
Let a digraph $D$ have a **height function** be a mapping $h:V(D)\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}$ such that $h(v)=h(u)+1$ for every arc $(u,v)\in A(D)$. An oriented forest is **grounded** if it admits a height function constant on the set of vertices of in-degree at least $2$. A digraph $F$ is **$\delta^+$-enforcible** if there exists $d(F)\in\mathbb{N}$ such that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least $d(F)$ contains a subdigraph isomorphic to $F$.

**KAMAK tree conjecture.** Every grounded forest is $\delta^+$-enforcible.

Hons et al. proved the necessary condition that every $\delta^+$-enforcible digraph is a grounded forest. The conjecture asserts sufficiency and is the main result proved in the paper, although the supplied status metadata marks it as open.

record.title: The maximal-gamma conjecture for minimal graphs
record.statement:
Let $\ell$ be a positive integer, let $G$ be an $\ell$-minimal graph, let $a$ be the vector used in the definition of $\gamma_{\ell-1}(G,a)$, and let $\bar{e}$ denote the all-ones edge vector. Let $\hat{\mathcal{K}}_{\ell+2,\ell-1}$ denote the specified class of sparse stretched cliques.

**Maximal-gamma conjecture.** For every positive integer $\ell$, the maximum value of $\gamma_{\ell-1}(G,a)$ among $\ell$-minimal graphs is attained by a sparse stretched clique $G \in \hat{\mathcal{K}}_{\ell+2,\ell-1}$ and $a \coloneqq \bar{e}$.

The observed 4-minimal examples motivate this conjecture, which predicts both the extremal graph class and the maximizing vector. No general proof or disproof is supplied in the source.

record.title: The toral rank and Carlsson conjectures for manifolds
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a closed connected manifold. Its **toral rank** is the largest integer $r$ such that $T^r$ acts almost freely on $M$, and, for a prime $p$, its **$p$-rank** is the largest integer $r$ such that $(\mathbb{Z}/p)^r$ acts freely on $M$.

**Toral rank and Carlsson conjectures.**

$$
\dim H^*(M,\mathbb{Q})\geq 2^{\operatorname{rank}(M)}
$$

and, for every prime $p$,

$$
\dim H^*(M,\mathbb{Z}/p)\geq 2^{\operatorname{rank}_p(M)}.
$$

These conjectures, attributed respectively to S. Halperin and G. Carlsson, relate the ranks of torus and elementary abelian group actions to the total cohomology of the manifold. Their resolution status is not specified in the source.

record.title: The stable Carlsson conjecture for manifolds
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a closed connected manifold, and let $\operatorname{rank}_p(M)$ denote the largest integer $r$ such that $(\mathbb{Z}/p)^r$ acts freely on $M$.

**Stable Carlsson conjecture.** There exists a constant $C$ such that, for every prime $p>C$,

$$
\dim H^*(M,\mathbb{Z}/p)\geq 2^{\operatorname{rank}_p(M)}.
$$

This is a weaker, stable version of Carlsson's conjecture: the asserted bound is required only for primes larger than a constant depending on $M$. The source does not specify whether it is open or resolved.

record.title: The low-degree extremal values conjecture for Sendov's refinement
record.statement: For $n\ge2$, let $r_n(\beta)$ be the maximum of $d(P,\beta)$ over $P\in S(\beta)$ of degree $n$, and let $c_n$ denote the corresponding sharp quadratic-refinement coefficient in the bound $d(P,\beta)\le1-c_n\beta(1-\beta)$. The experimentally conjectured values are listed in Table 2: $c_4=1/3$, $c_5=3/10$, $c_6=0.365121611819106$, $c_7=0.335088765359222$, and $c_8=(8-4\sqrt2)/7\approx0.334735107215374$. **The low-degree extremal values conjecture.** The conjectured values of $c_n$ listed in Table 2 are the correct values. record.title: The minimum-edge non-TRVG conjecture for $K_{3,5}$
record.statement:
Let a **transparent rectangle visibility graph (TRVG)** be a graph admitting a representation by axis-parallel rectangles in which two vertices are adjacent when their rectangles are visible to one another, and call a graph that has no such representation a **non-TRVG**. The complete bipartite graph $K_{3,5}$ has $15$ edges.

**Minimum-edge non-TRVG conjecture.** $K_{3,5}$ is a non-TRVG with the least number of edges.

The paper establishes that $K_{3,5}$ is a non-TRVG and reports that no non-TRVG with fewer than $15$ edges was found; the conjectured minimality remains open.

record.title: Ye–Lim's universal Toeplitz factorization conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $M\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$. Write $\mathrm{Toep}(M)$ for the minimal number of Toeplitz matrices whose product is $M$, and let $\mathrm{Toep}_n$ be the maximum of $\mathrm{Toep}(M)$ over all $n\times n$ matrices.

**Ye–Lim's conjecture.** For all $n\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
\mathrm{Toep}_n=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor+1.
$$

This asserts that the generic upper bound established by Ye and Lim holds for every matrix, not merely for generic matrices. The paper notes that the conjecture is true for $n=1,2$ but is disproved for $n=3$; the proposed replacement in odd dimensions appears later in the paper.

record.title: The p-optimality obstruction conjecture for analyzable proof systems
record.statement:
Let $Q$ be a propositional proof system. A proof system is **analyzable** when its associated proof-analysis problem admits the efficient analysis described in the paper, and it is **p-optimal** when it simulates every propositional proof system with polynomial overhead.

**Analyzability requires lower bounds or proofs that are hard to find.** For every propositional proof system $Q$, if $Q$ is analyzable, then $Q$ is not p-optimal.

This is a weaker proposed conclusion than non-optimality: failure of p-optimality permits explicit tautology families whose proofs are either long or short but computationally hard to find. The conjecture remains open in the source.

record.title: Greedy gossiping conjecture for temporal k-uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $n$ dons gossip in conference calls involving $k$ people, and let $m$ be a fixed number of calls smaller than the minimum number of calls needed for every don to know all the gossip. A call **maximises the amount of new gossip overheard** when it produces as much new gossip as possible at that point.

**Greedy gossiping conjecture.** The total number of gossip items known by the dons is maximal when every call maximises the amount of new gossip overheard.

This conjecture asks whether the greedy phenomenon proved in the paper's graph-call setting persists when calls form a temporal $k$-uniform hypergraph. The source poses it as a next question for fixed $k\geq 2$; no resolution is supplied here.

record.title: Bridge-number conjecture for spiral knots
record.statement:
For a spiral knot $S(p,q,\varepsilon)$, let $b(S(p,q,\varepsilon))$ denote its bridge number, and let $\min(p,q)$ be the minimum of its two integer parameters. **Bridge-number conjecture.** Every spiral knot satisfies

$$
b(S(p,q,\varepsilon))=\min(p,q).
$$

The formula holds for the examples and families discussed in the paper and is also known for torus knots. The conjecture proposes that it holds for all spiral knots; its general validity remains open.
